title: Refuse omarchy-update when invoked as root
head: a9a22c968119
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The command metadata still instructs consumers that update requires sudo
leads.consequence: `omarchy update --help --json` and `omarchy commands --json` continue advertising `requires_sudo: true` even though the new guard rejects EUID 0. A person or agent interpreting that boolean as requiring `sudo omarchy update` is sent straight to an error; this is exactly the advice-to-elevate trap identified in issue #13329. The dispatcher itself only records this flag and execs the binary without sudo, so removing the annotation does not remove per-step escalation. Omit the header instead of assigning false, which the metadata parser/lint rejects.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3; published as optional note

leads.summary: An earlier root-created update transcript still prevents the advised non-root retry
leads.consequence: If a previous root-run update left `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` owned by root, the root guard now tells its caller to update as a user, but `script -qefc` opens that same fixed pathname for writing before any update command or lock can run. On systems where that file is not writable by the user, `script` reports `cannot open /tmp/omarchy-update.log` and exits; every ordinary retry fails until the user repairs/removes the old log. This is a conditional migration/recovery defect, not a claim that every affected user has that file. Consider a private per-user transcript path (and its analyzer consumer) or explicit recovery guidance; an open #12957 also proposes a per-user runtime path.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing, not introduced by this PR; addressed by #12957 which is listed

leads.summary: The guard's invocation advice is skipped when the root caller lacks OMARCHY_PATH
leads.consequence: For a root caller whose environment lacks `OMARCHY_PATH` (such as a sudo invocation with that variable removed), `omarchy_security_require_source_root` returns 1 under `set -e` before the new EUID branch. It emits only `OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.` rather than explaining to run as the user, despite the new user-facing message. Root work is still stopped. Arrange root advice after sanitization but before this environment-dependent check, without relaxing source-root validation for permitted callers.

leads.summary: On hosts without user namespaces the new regression test passes even if root is not rejected
leads.consequence: The fallback only searches for a guard header and a literal error string; it never requires an `exit 1` or runs the root path. In an isolated LC_ALL=C run with `unshare` unavailable, replacing the guard's `exit 1` with a no-op still yields exit 0 and the same TAP PASS. This plausible mutant would run all update phases as root if a root caller reaches it. Make the fallback assert the executable refusal or run an identity-injected, completely stubbed boundary fixture; keep all package, sudo, hook, and logging writes stubbed.

leads.summary: Open #13660 independently adds the same root guard and the same test pathname, requiring explicit conflict resolution
leads.consequence: #13660 is divergent (compare status), not stacked. Its own diff inserts a different guard after the security prologue and adds a different `test/shell.d/update-refuse-root-test.sh`. Three-way merging the two PRs' files against #13660's base leaves conflict markers in both the updater and the new test, even though GitHub reports #13660 mergeable into its own base. If resolved by keeping both guards, root still exits at the first one and the second guard is dead; if resolved by choosing #13660's test, the current PR's namespace exercise is lost. Coordinate and retain one guard and one test.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus merge-tree and coordinator diff read; published in related PRs block

leads.summary: Open #12796's root-update compatibility path is negated by this guard
leads.consequence: #12796 explicitly intends to make `sudo omarchy update` work by running yay as `SUDO_USER` when EUID 0 and resolving the desktop session on root-started shell restart. These changes are not stacked with this PR, and if both merge the outer root invocation exits before reaching either change, while the new yay root branch is dead from this route. This is a product-direction conflict, not a claim that its standalone helper tests fail; choose one policy or revise the other PR accordingly.
leads.triage: corroborated; published with Opus self-check narrowing (source-root check already stops plain sudo)

limits: The root preflight itself was not executed without the guard: that path would run unstubbed package, sudo, mise and post-update commands. The isolated fallback and negative control exercised only static code and stubs; source analysis establishes the other claims. The upstream util-linux reference file was fetched from upstream default branch rather than a distro version pin; confirm the distro's script.c implementation if relying on nonstandard open modes.

flags.claim: Test scope: ... real sudo not run.
flags.why: The host's real /usr/bin/sudo binary was executed, without privileges, inside the sandbox's user namespace, and the draft quotes its output (lines 192-202). What did not happen is sudo running with root privileges. The draft inherited this from my own report's Limitations line ('No real sudo, pkexec or root'), which is inconsistent with my runs.

flags.claim: omarchy-channel-set ends by running omarchy-update, so as root it switches packages, then fails and suggests a rerun that fails the same way.
flags.why: The qualifier 'with OMARCHY_PATH kept' is lost. omarchy-channel-set has the same prologue, including omarchy_security_require_source_root, so under plain sudo (env_reset) it stops at that check before switching anything. The half-finished switch happens only for the sudo -E / sudo -i / su shape. My test run exported OMARCHY_PATH.

flags.claim: #12796: opposite approach; makes root runs work via SUDO_USER in the helpers, which this guard would make unreachable.
flags.why: (a) Per #12796's body, SUDO_USER is used only in omarchy-update-aur-pkgs and omarchy-restart-shell. omarchy-update-dev and omarchy-update-available instead default OMARCHY_PATH to /usr/share/omarchy. (b) #12796 targets plain sudo, where OMARCHY_PATH is unset. On quattro that shape is already stopped by the existing source-root check before any helper runs, with or without this PR, so it is not this guard that makes those paths unreachable. This guard stops only the OMARCHY_PATH-kept shapes. (c) The helpers stay reachable when called directly; only the route through omarchy-update is closed.

Wrong attribution for three of the four entries. Only #13660 references #13329. #11479 says 'Addresses #11257'. #12957 references #11630 and #11204 (it was opened on 2026-09-22, before #13329 was filed on 2026-09-26). #12796 references no issue.
Stale number. It was 261 at the intake tip b421b1b. quattro is now 8b4eae66 and the count is 263. The substance (a very old branch) stands.

flags.claim: With exit 1 replaced by :, the test passes: the update continues and the real sudo -k fails, giving the nonzero status.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. sudo -k fails only because the suite runs as a normal user, whose namespace root cannot use sudo. For a real-root runner, sudo -k would succeed and the update would continue. The reproducer's Caution covers the root case, but the visible sentence reads as unconditional. Minor.

flags.claim: Verified (sandbox, ...): Root with OMARCHY_PATH kept (sudo -E, sudo -i, su) ...; the menu and first-run callers launch the update as the session user.
flags.why: Nitpick. The sandbox verified the OMARCHY_PATH-kept shape (env with OMARCHY_PATH in a namespace mapped to root). Mapping that shape to sudo -E, sudo -i and su comes from reading the source, not from running those commands. The menu and first-run item also comes from reading the source, not the sandbox.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Plain `sudo omarchy update` (#13329) never reaches the new message, and the new test passes with the guard's `exit 1` removed.

### Plain `sudo` exits before the guard

sudo's default `env_reset` drops `OMARCHY_PATH`, so the source-root check (line 19) exits with `OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.` before the guard (line 24). The output is unchanged from the base.

**Suggested change:** move the block above `omarchy_security_require_source_root` and test without `OMARCHY_PATH`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at a9a22c9)</summary>

# Reproducer: plain `sudo` never reaches the new refusal

Finding: with Arch's default sudo (`env_reset`), `OMARCHY_PATH` is not passed
through, so `omarchy_security_require_source_root` (line 19) exits before the
new `EUID == 0` block (line 24) and prints `OMARCHY_PATH does not match this
Omarchy command.` instead of the new guidance.

## Test (fails at the PR head, a9a22c9)

Save as `test/shell.d/update-refuse-root-reset-env-test.sh` and run
`bash test/shell.d/update-refuse-root-reset-env-test.sh` as a normal user.
It uses the repository's sudo-boundary fixture, so sudo and every update step
are stand-ins; nothing real is updated, even on a regression.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
source "$SHELL_TEST_DIR/fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh"
copy_boundary_file bin/omarchy-update

if ! unshare --user --map-root-user true 2>/dev/null; then
  skip "no unprivileged user namespace; skipping the root refusal"
  exit 0
fi

# Every update step is a stand-in that records itself; sudo is the fixture's.
steps="$boundary_tmp/steps"
for step in omarchy-update-lock omarchy-update-requires-free-space omarchy-update-pkg-prune \
  omarchy-snapshot omarchy-update-stay-awake omarchy-update-dev omarchy-update-keyring \
  omarchy-update-system-pkgs omarchy-migrate omarchy-hook omarchy-update-mise \
  omarchy-update-aur-pkgs omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs omarchy-update-analyze-logs \
  omarchy-update-status omarchy-update-restart; do
  rm -f "$SUDO_TEST_ROOT/bin/$step"
  printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "${0##*/} euid=$EUID" >>"%s"\n' "$steps" >"$SUDO_TEST_ROOT/bin/$step"
  chmod +x "$SUDO_TEST_ROOT/bin/$step"
done

run_as_root() {
  : >"$steps"
  : >"$SUDO_TEST_LOG"
  status=0
  output=$(unshare --user --map-root-user env "$@" OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1 \
    "$SUDO_TEST_ROOT/bin/omarchy-update" -y 2>&1) || status=$?
}

# sudo -E, sudo -i and su keep OMARCHY_PATH.
run_as_root
(( status != 0 )) || fail "root with OMARCHY_PATH is refused" "$output"
[[ ! -s $steps && ! -s $SUDO_TEST_LOG ]] || fail "root with OMARCHY_PATH runs no step and no sudo" "$(cat "$steps" "$SUDO_TEST_LOG")"
[[ $output == *"not under sudo"* ]] || fail "root with OMARCHY_PATH is told to run as the user" "$output"
pass "root with OMARCHY_PATH is refused before any step"

# Plain sudo resets the environment (env_reset), so OMARCHY_PATH is gone.
run_as_root -u OMARCHY_PATH
(( status != 0 )) || fail "root under sudo's reset environment is refused" "$output"
[[ ! -s $steps ]] || fail "root under sudo's reset environment runs no step" "$(cat "$steps")"
[[ $output == *"not under sudo"* ]] || fail "root under sudo's reset environment is told to run as the user" "$output"
pass "root under sudo's reset environment is told to run as the user"
```

## Actual output at the PR head (a9a22c9), exit status 1

stdout:

```
ok - root with OMARCHY_PATH is refused before any step
```

stderr:

```
OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.
not ok - root under sudo's reset environment is told to run as the user
```

## Actual output with the same 9-line block moved above `omarchy_security_require_source_root "$0"`, exit status 0

stdout:

```
ok - root with OMARCHY_PATH is refused before any step
ok - root under sudo's reset environment is told to run as the user
```

stderr: empty.

## Same result through the dispatcher

From the root of the PR head checkout, with the environment sudo's
`env_reset` leaves (no `OMARCHY_PATH`), inside a user namespace mapped to root:

```bash
unshare --user --map-root-user env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin HOME=/root TERM=dumb \
  LOGNAME=root USER=root SHELL=/bin/bash SUDO_USER=user SUDO_UID=1000 SUDO_GID=1000 \
  "SUDO_COMMAND=/usr/bin/omarchy update -y" "$PWD/bin/omarchy" update -y
```

Actual output (stderr), exit status 1, identical at the PR head and at its
base c5b4db7:

```
OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.
```

With `OMARCHY_PATH="$PWD"` added (the `sudo -E` / `sudo -i` / `su` shape), the
PR head prints:

```
Error: run omarchy-update as your user, not under sudo.
It asks for a password when a step needs privilege.
```

Environment: bubblewrap sandbox, bash 5.3.15, util-linux 2.42.3 `unshare`.

</details>

### Test passes when the guard does not stop the update

With `exit 1` replaced by `:`, the test passes as a normal user: the update continues and the real `sudo -k` fails with a nonzero status. On a regression it runs the real update script, not the sudo stand-ins.

**Suggested change:** build the test on `fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh` and assert that no step or sudo call ran.

<details><summary>Reproducer (passes with the guard disabled)</summary>

# Reproducer: the new test still passes when the guard does not stop the update

Finding: the namespace branch of `test/shell.d/update-refuse-root-test.sh`
only checks for a nonzero status and the message text. With the guard's
`exit 1` removed, the update prints the message and carries on; the real
`/usr/bin/sudo -k` then fails inside the user namespace, which supplies the
nonzero status, so the test still reports `ok`.

Caution: run this only as a normal user. With the guard disabled, the test
executes the real update script (not the repository's sudo-boundary stand-ins),
so as real root it would go on to a real update.

## Steps (from the root of a scratch copy of the PR head, a9a22c9)

```bash
sed -i '/not under sudo/,/^fi$/ s/^  exit 1$/  :/' bin/omarchy-update
bash test/shell.d/update-refuse-root-test.sh
```

The `sed` changes exactly one line:

```diff
 if (( EUID == 0 )); then
   echo "Error: run omarchy-update as your user, not under sudo." >&2
   echo "It asks for a password when a step needs privilege." >&2
-  exit 1
+  :
 fi
```

## Actual output, exit status 0

```
ok - omarchy-update refuses to run as root so mise stays user-owned
```

## Why it passes

The command the test runs, against the mutated script:

```bash
unshare --user --map-root-user env OMARCHY_PATH="$PWD" OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1 \
  /usr/bin/bash -p "$PWD/bin/omarchy-update" -y
```

Actual stderr, exit status 1:

```
Error: run omarchy-update as your user, not under sudo.
It asks for a password when a step needs privilege.
sudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
sudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
sudo: PERM_SUDOERS: setresuid(-1, 1, -1): Invalid argument
sudo: unable to open /etc/sudoers: Invalid argument
sudo: error initializing audit plugin sudoers_audit
sudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
sudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
sudo: PERM_SUDOERS: setresuid(-1, 1, -1): Invalid argument
sudo: unable to open /etc/sudoers: Invalid argument
sudo: error initializing audit plugin sudoers_audit
Could not invalidate cached sudo authorization.
```

## The sudo-boundary version catches it

The test in the other reproducer (`update-refuse-root-reset-env-test.sh`,
built on `test/shell.d/fixtures/sudo-boundary-test.sh`) run against the same
mutated script, exit status 1:

```
Error: run omarchy-update as your user, not under sudo.
It asks for a password when a step needs privilege.
not ok - root with OMARCHY_PATH is refused
```

Environment: bubblewrap sandbox, bash 5.3.15, util-linux 2.42.3 `unshare`.

</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #13660: same guard, also after the source-root check, test is grep-only; over 260 commits behind `quattro`, bundles an unrelated Windows VM change, and adds the same test file path (add/add conflict with this PR).

Related open PRs that reference other issues:
- #11479 (for #11257): same guard (earliest, 2026-09-12); merges cleanly with this PR, which would leave two guards.
- #12957 (for #11630, #11204): mainly moves the update transcript out of `/tmp`; also adds a root guard with this PR's first message line, after the cleanup traps. Merges cleanly with this PR, which would leave two guards.
- #12796: opposite approach; makes root runs work via `SUDO_USER` in `omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` and `omarchy-restart-shell`. With this PR those paths are no longer reached through `omarchy-update`, though on `quattro` plain `sudo` already stops at the source-root check.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox, root simulated with `unshare --user --map-root-user`):
- Root with `OMARCHY_PATH` kept is refused before any sudo call, trap, log or update step; at the base, all update steps ran with euid 0. From source, `sudo -E`, `sudo -i` and `su` keep `OMARCHY_PATH`.
- As a normal user, all update steps still run. From source, the menu and first-run callers launch the update as the session user.
- `omarchy commands --check` passes.

**Optional notes:**
- `omarchy-channel-set` ends by running `omarchy-update`, so as root with `OMARCHY_PATH` kept it switches packages, then fails and suggests a rerun that fails the same way. A root refusal at its start, as in `omarchy-plymouth-set`, avoids the half-finished switch.
- `requires-sudo=true` on `omarchy-update` is what led to the `sudo` call in #13329. Dropping it, or clarifying in `agents/skills/command-metadata.md` that it means the command prompts for sudo itself, avoids the contradiction with the new refusal.
- Run as root (namespace), six existing update and sudo-boundary tests fail at this head but pass at the base; this matters only if the suite is run as root.
</details>
